- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.1), model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; smooth forecast curve by reducing volatility amplitude.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% per day for first 7 days if sentiment is weak.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative values), model should not forecast upward trend; cap forecast at prior 10-day moving average.
- When true outcome drops below 60% of prior 10-day high, model often fails to recognize structural weakness; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
